question: Which federal agencies does each executive order put to work?
answer: The 509 Trump executive orders with agency maps (January 20, 2017 to September 29, 2026) put 163 federal agencies and offices to work. The Justice Department is named in the most orders (153), then the Office of Management and Budget (147) and the Department of Homeland Security (139).
uncertain: A count means the agency appears somewhere on the order's map: as the lead, a partner, or an office that must be consulted. It is not a count of orders the agency leads.
The maps are this library's reading of each order's text, not an official government list.
0 order(s) on file have no agency map yet, so they are not counted.
Orders signed after September 29, 2026 appear here only once their note and map are filed.
Whether an order is still in force (or was revoked later) is not tracked on this page; the count includes first-term orders that were later revoked.

tree.name: United States
tree.about: The federal sovereign — issuer of the currency and the debt, and the ultimate parent of the whole group.

tree.name: Legislative Branch
tree.about: Congress and its own agencies — writes the charters that create and dissolve every other entity.

tree.name: Legislative support agencies
tree.about: The agencies Congress owns and runs.

tree.name: Judicial Branch
tree.about: The federal courts — where a charter, a dissolution, or a conservatorship gets tested.

tree.name: Executive Branch
tree.about: The President and the operating group — where the 2025–26 reorganization is happening.

tree.name: Executive Office of the President
tree.about: The President's own staff agencies (created by the 1939 Reorganization Act).

tree.name: Office of Management & Budget
tree.about: Controls the money and the org chart across the whole executive group (Bureau of the Budget, 1921).

tree.name: Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs (OIRA)
tree.about: OMB office established by the Paperwork Reduction Act; reviews significant regulatory actions and government-wide information policy.

tree.name: Domestic Policy Council
tree.about: EO 12859 council for coordinating domestic policy and monitoring implementation across executive departments and agencies.

tree.name: Office of the National Cyber Director (ONCD)
tree.about: Statutory EOP office advising the President and coordinating national cybersecurity strategy and policy.

tree.name: National Economic Council
tree.about: Coordinates domestic and international economic policy inside the Executive Office of the President.

tree.name: Presidential Working Group on Digital Asset Markets
tree.about: EO 14178 interagency policy body for digital assets, stablecoins, market structure, and the proposed stockpile.

tree.name: Office of National Drug Control Policy
DOGE
tree.about: Department of Government Efficiency — a re-flagged US Digital Service (USDS, 2014), re-chartered to run the dissolutions.

tree.name: Task Force to Eliminate Fraud
tree.about: EO 14395 interagency task force chaired by the Vice President for benefit-program identity, eligibility, pre-payment, and fraud controls.

tree.name: Executive Departments
tree.about: The 15 statutory departments — the wholly-owned operating subsidiaries.

tree.name: Dept of the Treasury
tree.about: The money parent — issues the debt, runs disbursement, custodies the new digital-asset vehicles, and chairs the councils that watch the whole financial system.

tree.name: IRS
tree.about: Revenue collection.

tree.name: Bureau of the Fiscal Service
tree.about: Runs the disbursement rails and the public debt (merger of BPD + FMS).

tree.name: OCC
tree.about: Charters and supervises national banks — the chartering desk for the banking layer.

tree.name: Office of Terrorism & Financial Intelligence (TFI)
tree.about: Treasury's national-security arm: policy, intelligence, regulation, enforcement, sanctions, illicit-finance controls, and asset-forfeiture administration.

tree.name: Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC)
tree.about: Administers and enforces Treasury financial sanctions: designations, lists, blocking, licensing, compliance, and civil enforcement.

tree.name: FinCEN
tree.about: Treasury bureau administering the Bank Secrecy Act and financial-intelligence framework for money laundering, terrorist financing, and other financial crimes.

tree.name: CDFI Fund
tree.about: Channels capital into community development financial institutions — named for reduction March 2025.

tree.name: Federal Financing Bank
tree.about: A Treasury-owned bank that lends to other federal agencies and buys their debt.

tree.name: Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC)
tree.about: A Treasury-chaired council of all the financial regulators.

tree.name: CFIUS
tree.about: Treasury-chaired committee that screens foreign investment for national-security risk.

tree.name: Strategic Bitcoin Reserve
tree.about: Permanent Treasury-held BTC reserve, chartered by EO, seeded with forfeited bitcoin. Still fighting to become statute.

tree.name: US Digital Asset Stockpile
tree.about: Sister vehicle holding non-bitcoin forfeited digital assets under Treasury.

tree.name: Dept of State
tree.about: Absorbed USAID's surviving functions in 2025 after that agency was cut ~95%.

tree.name: USAID (remnant)
tree.about: Cut ~95%; what survived was folded into State.

tree.name: Dept of Justice
tree.about: Runs federal forfeiture — the pipeline that fed seized bitcoin into the new Treasury reserve.

tree.name: Bureau of Prisons
tree.about: Runs the federal prisons.

tree.name: Dept of Health & Human Services
tree.about: Reorganized in 2025 — sub-agencies dissolved and rolled into a new survivor (HEW, 1953).

tree.name: CMS
tree.about: Runs Medicare & Medicaid.

tree.name: SAMHSA
tree.about: Dissolved March 2025 ($8.1B, ~900 staff) into the new AHA.

tree.name: HRSA (parts)
tree.about: Partly dissolved / rolled into AHA.

tree.name: Dept of Homeland Security
tree.about: Internal offices shut down March 2025 (Civil Rights & Civil Liberties, two ombudsmen).

tree.name: Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA)
tree.about: DHS operational agency for federal cybersecurity, critical-infrastructure security, threat sharing, and resilience support.

tree.name: US Coast Guard
tree.about: A military service and armed-forces branch inside DHS — 14 USC 101 dates the named Coast Guard to 28 Jan 1915.

tree.name: Dept of Education
tree.about: Marked for wind-down in 2025; functions being dispersed to other departments.

tree.name: Federal Student Aid
tree.about: Performance-based organization that runs the federal student-aid programs and the student-loan operating book.

tree.name: Dept of Defense
tree.about: Largest operating subsidiary by budget and headcount (National Security Act).

tree.name: Defense intelligence (NSA · DIA · NGA · NRO)
tree.about: The combat-support intelligence agencies inside Defense, not the CIA.

tree.name: Dept of Commerce
tree.about: Home of the new Investment Accelerator — the office the Sovereign Wealth Fund is actually operating through.

tree.name: Bureau of Industry & Security
tree.about: Runs export controls — the chip-export chokepoint.

tree.name: Minority Business Development Agency
tree.about: Named for elimination March 2025.

tree.name: US Investment Accelerator
tree.about: New Commerce office (EO 14255) to fast-track $1B+ investments — the real mechanism behind the decentralized 'sovereign wealth fund'.

tree.name: Dept of Energy
tree.about: Owns the nuclear-weapons complex and the national labs — but private companies run them.

tree.name: NNSA
tree.about: National Nuclear Security Administration — a semi-autonomous agency inside Energy.

tree.name: Idaho National Lab
tree.about: The reactor proving ground.

tree.name: FERC
tree.about: Independent energy regulator housed within Energy.

tree.name: Dept of Agriculture
tree.about: Runs its own lending and insurance corporations.

tree.name: Dept of Labor
tree.about: Holds the unemployment system's trust fund.

tree.name: Dept of the Interior
tree.about: Public lands and natural resources.

tree.name: Independent agencies & regulators
tree.about: Subsidiaries with special governance — boards, fixed terms, insulation from direct control.

tree.name: SEC
tree.about: Securities regulator — the rules letting the register go on-chain (the Ledger track).

tree.name: CFTC
tree.about: Derivatives / commodities regulator — the crypto turf fight.

tree.name: FHFA
tree.about: Regulator AND conservator of Fannie & Freddie since 2008 — drawn here as their parent-of-record WHILE the conservatorship lasts.

tree.name: Fannie Mae
tree.about: Federally chartered mortgage giant, private shareholders — in FHFA conservatorship since Sep 2008. Treasury holds senior preferred stock + warrants for 79.9% of the common.

tree.name: Freddie Mac
tree.about: Sister GSE, also in FHFA conservatorship since Sep 2008 — same Treasury stake, same limbo.

tree.name: NCUA
tree.about: Credit-union regulator — part-corporation.

tree.name: CFPB
tree.about: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau — funding cut off and gutted in 2025.

tree.name: United States International Trade Commission (USITC)
tree.about: Independent, nonpartisan, quasi-judicial trade agency: adjudication, trade analysis, and maintenance of the Harmonized Tariff Schedule.

tree.name: Federal Mediation & Conciliation Service
tree.about: Named for elimination March 2025 — courts vacated the shutdown (Dec 2025); staff reinstated, fully operational again.

tree.name: Institute of Museum & Library Services
tree.about: Named for elimination March 2025; government withdrew its appeal in the Apr 2026 settlement — staff returned, agency restored.

tree.name: US Agency for Global Media
tree.about: Runs Voice of America — named for elimination March 2025.

tree.name: US Institute of Peace
tree.about: Targeted Feb 2025. A district court ruled for USIP in May 2025, but the D.C. Circuit stayed that ruling on June 27, 2025. Its website now presents it as the 'Donald J. Trump Institute of Peace'.

tree.name: Inter-American Foundation
tree.about: Gutted Feb 2025; reinstated by court. The D.C. Circuit denied the government's request to pause that order on June 5, 2025 (Aviel v. Gor); the appeal's final outcome is not yet checked.

tree.name: US African Development Foundation
tree.about: Staff and grants stripped 2025; slated out of the 2026 budget.

tree.name: US Interagency Council on Homelessness
tree.about: Named for elimination March 2025.

tree.name: Government corporations
tree.about: Entities literally chartered as corporations — own charter, own board, own balance sheet.

tree.name: USPS
tree.about: The Postal Service — legally an INDEPENDENT ESTABLISHMENT of the executive branch (39 USC 201), not a chartered corporation; sues and is sued in its own name (Post Office Dept, 1792).

tree.name: Amtrak
tree.about: National Railroad Passenger Corporation — statutorily 'not a department, agency, or instrumentality of the United States'; the Supreme Court says otherwise.

tree.name: TVA
tree.about: Self-funding federal power corporation, off the appropriations books.

tree.name: FDIC
tree.about: Deposit insurer with its own fund built from bank premiums — a corporation inside the regulatory layer.

tree.name: Export-Import Bank
tree.about: Wholly-owned export-credit corporation (EO 6581, 2 Feb 1934; Export-Import Bank Act of 1945).

tree.name: US International Development Finance Corporation
tree.about: Wholly-owned development-finance corporation; BUILD Act successor to OPIC.

tree.name: Millennium Challenge Corporation
tree.about: A foreign-aid corporation with its own board.

tree.name: Presidio Trust
tree.about: Runs the Presidio of San Francisco as a self-funding corporation.

tree.name: Intelligence Community (coordination overlay)
tree.about: NOT an entity — a defined coordination construct (50 USC 3003): no charter of its own, no balance sheet, no employees. The 18 members are executive-branch agencies and components of Defense, Justice, Treasury, DHS, State, and Energy.

tree.name: Office of the DNI
tree.about: Coordinates the community; does not own most of it.

tree.name: CIA
tree.about: An independent agency reporting to the President.

tree.name: The Federal Reserve System
tree.about: The central bank — chartered by Congress (Federal Reserve Act, 23 Dec 1913) but not owned or run by the executive. Public head, private body.

tree.name: Board of Governors
tree.about: The public head — unambiguously a federal agency: 7 governors, Senate-confirmed (restructured & renamed by the Banking Act of 1935). Supervises the Banks, approves their presidents, controls their budgets.

tree.name: The 12 Federal Reserve Banks
tree.about: Regional banks that are private corporations, their stock held by the member commercial banks (opened 16 Nov 1914).

tree.name: 2 · New York
tree.about: The first among equals — runs the System Open Market Account and the trading desk.

tree.name: FOMC
tree.about: The rate-setting committee — the modern statutory FOMC comes from the Banking Act of 1935; first meeting 18 Mar 1936. 12 voters: the 7 governors + the NY Fed president (permanent) + 4 rotating Bank presidents.

tree.name: Federally chartered / quasi-official
tree.about: Bodies Congress chartered but does not run — the group's penumbra.

tree.name: Smithsonian Institution
tree.about: A trust instrumentality of the US — a museum empire run by a Board of Regents (the Chief Justice, the VP, and members of Congress — genuinely tri-branch).

tree.name: Woodrow Wilson International Center
tree.about: A Smithsonian-affiliated think tank — hit in 2025, core functions preserved; running fellowships again by spring 2026.

tree.name: Chartered, not owned
tree.about: Federally CHARTERED but privately owned, funded, and governed — a congressional charter alone does not put you in the group.

tree.name: Corporation for Public Broadcasting
tree.about: A private DC nonprofit — FEDERALLY FUNDED (appropriations pass through it to public media).

tree.name: Supranational memberships
tree.about: Entities the US does not own but is a member/shareholder of — consolidation pointing UP and OUT.

tree.name: The UN system
tree.about: The US is a member — and in 2025 began withdrawing from parts.

tree.name: United Nations
tree.about: The US is a founding member and permanent Security Council seat.

tree.name: World Health Organization
tree.about: The US ordered withdrawal in Jan 2025.

tree.name: UNESCO
tree.about: The US withdrew again in 2025.

tree.name: World Trade Organization
tree.about: Trade rules — sidelined by the 2025 tariff turn (GATT, 1948).

orders.title: Declaring a National Emergency To Secure the United States Bulk-Power System
orders.note: vault:03 - Executive Orders/2026-08-26 - EO 14421 - Declaring a National Emergency To Secure the United States Bulk-Power System.md
orders.gist: The President declares a fresh IEEPA/NEA national emergency concerning foreign supply of bulk-power-system electric equipment. Energy holds the transaction determination, legacy-equipment conditions, mitigation, licensing, replacement, rule, equipment-identification, procurement-recommendation, and congressional-report leashes. The Office of Management and Budget coordinates the section 2(a) determination, while equipment-risk recommendations route to the President through the Assistant to the President for National Security Affairs. OFR published the order as EO 14421 (91 FR 55995; FR Doc. 2026-17843; signed 2026-08-26, published 2026-08-31). The earlier White House 14420 collision is closed.
orders.status_on_map: national emergency declared · EO 14421 confirmed on the Federal Register · transaction prohibitions require an Energy determination · rules, equipment actions, FAR revisions, and reports not proved issued

orders.title: Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Ensuring Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials
orders.note: vault:03 - Executive Orders/2026-07-20 - EO 14415 - Securing America's Defense Supply Chains and Ensuring Domestic Acquisition of Critical Materials.md
orders.gist: The Secretary of War — join Dept of Defense — holds the 10 U.S.C. § 4872 waiver leash. From January 1, 2027, (c)(1) waivers stop except under an accepted mitigation plan; (e) waivers follow that plan or a request to the National Security Advisor. Defense must develop mapping policy and implementing regulations, including an indentured Bill of Materials. Semiannual reports to the National Security Advisor may carry a classified annex. That annex is to a report, not an attached order. A waiver restriction is not a completed cutoff of all foreign material. Project Vault and Export-Import or Development Finance Corporation-financed sources are carved out.
orders.status_on_map: waiver restriction dated 2027-01-01 · mapping regulations and reports directed, not proved · classified annex is to the report

Treasury and the Office of Management and Budget shall review the Executive Order 12866 exemption for certain tax regulations. A review is not a rescission. A directed delay is not an Internal Revenue Code amendment.

The Office of National Drug Control Policy funds and staffs it and performs Federal Advisory Committee Act presidential functions except sections 6 and 14. The Commission must file a 90-day interim and a final report by October 1, 2017 unless the Chair extends. It terminates 30 days after the final report unless extended. A commission is not a department. A report is not a statute.

orders.title: Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth
orders.note: vault:03 - Executive Orders/2017-03-28 - EO 13783 - Promoting Energy Independence and Economic Growth.md
orders.gist: Agency heads must review actions that potentially burden domestic energy, with particular attention to oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear, and send the Office of Management and Budget a 45-day plan, a 120-day draft report, and a 180-day final report with suspend/revise/rescind recommendations. This paper revokes four Obama-era energy and climate presidential actions, rescinds two Climate Action Plan reports, and directs the Council on Environmental Quality to rescind its 2016 greenhouse-gas NEPA guidance. The Environmental Protection Agency must review the Clean Power Plan and related rules. The Interagency Working Group on Social Cost of Greenhouse Gases is disbanded and its technical documents withdrawn; agencies must use OMB Circular A-4 of 17 September 2003. Interior is directed to lift the Order 3338 coal-leasing moratorium. A review is not an issued replacement rule. Disbanding a working group is not a statute.

Agency heads have 180 days to send the Director a proposed reorganization of their own shop. The Director must publish a Federal Register notice inviting public suggestions, then, within 180 days after that comment close, send the President a proposed plan that may recommend eliminating unnecessary agencies, components, or programs, merging functions, and any legislation needed to do that. A proposed plan is not an organic-act repeal. A recommendation to eliminate an agency is not a completed close.

orders.title: Protecting the Nation From Foreign Terrorist Entry Into the United States
orders.note: vault:03 - Executive Orders/2017-03-06 - EO 13780 - Protecting the Nation From Foreign Terrorist Entry Into the United States.md
orders.gist: This paper revokes EO 13769 as of 16 March 2017 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time and replaces it. Under 8 U.S.C. §§ 1182(f) and 1185(a) it suspends for 90 days entry of nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, and Yemen who are outside the United States, had no valid visa at 17:00 e.s.t. on 27 January 2017, and have no valid visa on the effective date, subject to listed exceptions and case-by-case waivers. Iraq is dropped from the pause and given extra scrutiny, including Defense consultation. Homeland Security holds a worldwide information review due in 20 days that is supposed to feed a later proclamation. State holds a 120-day USRAP travel halt and a 50,000 FY2017 cap; the Syrian-only refugee bar is not restated. A 90-day pause is not a statute. Those 90- and 120-day clocks ran. A later proclamation is a sibling, not this paper.

research.title: Executive orders: full texts and saved research notes
research.answer: Saved executive-order records keep signature, publication and later implementation as separate dates. Full legal text and official source links remain available. A signed order does not establish funding, implementation or measured effect.

research.title: One map to browse all saved federal research
research.answer: This is a navigation hub, not a finding: it puts Katie's saved government research, a map of federal bodies, congressional committees, confirmed changes and known gaps in one place, while keeping each source's evidence separate.
